title: Peaking Factor — Maximum Day Demand
applicability: Higher peaking factors for smaller systems and warmer climates. Lower for large systems and conservation-oriented communities. 10 States Standards recommends MDD = 2.0 × ADD if data unavailable.

title: Peaking Factor — Peak Hour Demand

PF_PHD.description: Peak hour peaking factor (2.5–4.0 × ADD typical)

applicability: Alternatively expressed as PHD = PF_hourly × MDD where PF_hourly = 1.5–2.0. Peak hour demand governs pipe sizing for normal (non-fire) operation.

title: Available Fire Flow from Hydrant Test

Q_avail.description: Available fire flow at minimum residual pressure

P_residual_min.description: Minimum allowable residual pressure (20 psi / 140 kPa)

P_residual_test.description: Measured residual pressure during test flow

applicability: Standard hydrant flow test analysis. Exponent 0.54 corresponds to Hazen-Williams relationship (Q ∝ ΔH^0.54). Results valid for the test location only; varies by network configuration and source capacity.

title: Chlorine Residual Decay (First-Order)

k_b.description: Bulk decay coefficient (0.1–1.0 per day typical)

applicability: Bulk decay only. Total decay includes wall demand: overall k = k_b + k_w where k_w depends on pipe material and condition. Old unlined cast iron has highest wall demand. Decay is temperature-dependent — doubles approximately every 10°C rise.

title: Hardy-Cross Method — Flow Correction

hf_i.description: Head loss in pipe i (with sign: positive for CW assumed direction)

n.description: Flow exponent (1.852 for Hazen-Williams, 2.0 for Darcy-Weisbach)

applicability: Iterative method for analyzing looped networks. Apply ΔQ to all pipes in the loop; iterate until ΔQ → 0 for all loops simultaneously. Historical method — modern software uses Newton-Raphson gradient algorithm, but Hardy-Cross remains useful for understanding.

title: Equivalent Pipe for Parallel Mains
equation: C_eq^1.852 × D_eq^4.87 = Σ(Ci^1.852 × Di^4.87)  (for same length)
applicability: For parallel pipes of the same length: combined capacity = sum of individual capacities at the same head loss. Simplifies analysis when replacing with a single equivalent pipe.

title: Infrastructure Leakage Index (ILI)

ILI.description: Infrastructure Leakage Index — ratio of actual to unavoidable losses

UARL.description: Unavoidable Annual Real Losses = (18 × Lm + 0.8 × Nc + 25 × Lp) × P

applicability: ILI = 1.0 = theoretical minimum loss. ILI < 2: excellent. 2–4: good. 4–8: fair. > 8: poor. UARL formula (IWA): Lm = length of mains (km), Nc = number of service connections, Lp = total length of service pipes (km), P = average operating pressure (m).
source: IWA Water Loss Task Force, Lambert et al. (1999)

title: Pressure Zone Elevation Range

ΔZ_zone.description: Maximum elevation range within one pressure zone

P_max.description: Maximum acceptable static pressure (550 kPa / 80 psi typical)

P_min.description: Minimum acceptable pressure during peak demand (275 kPa / 40 psi)

applicability: Example: (550-275)/9.81 = 28 m. With head losses in the system, practical zone range is 30–40 m. Wider zone ranges are acceptable with careful pressure management (PRVs at high-pressure locations).
